Get a token callback for one Fabric service

Source: R/backend__fabric.R
oauth_db_fabric.Rd

Call a fabricQueryR function with the visitor's credentials for one Fabric service. This helper supplies a token callback: a function fabricQueryR calls when it needs a current access token. Use oauth_db_fabric_api() when working with several services or resource objects such as Lakehouses.

Usage

oauth_db_fabric(
  authorization,
  service = c("fabric", "sql", "dax", "kql", "onelake", "graphql"),
  target = .odb_fabric_profile(service)$target,
  required_scopes = NULL,
  min_valid_for = 60,
  session = shiny::getDefaultReactiveDomain()
)

Arguments

authorization

Function providing the visitor's current sign-in authorization. Pass auth$connection from shinyOAuth without parentheses. To select a saved account, use a function calling auth$connection(id).

service

One of "fabric", "sql", "dax", "kql", "onelake", or "graphql".

target

Token target name. Defaults to the service's preset target. Use NULL if the authorization has no named targets.

required_scopes

Additional permissions to check. NULL uses the service's read/query defaults.

min_valid_for

Minimum remaining token lifetime, in seconds, when obtaining a token. Use 0 to accept any unexpired token.

session

The visitor's Shiny session. Usually inferred when you create the helper inside server().

Value

A reactive function, such as callback. Calling callback() returns the token callback to pass to a fabricQueryR function, as token = callback() in the example below.

Details

Create the helper inside server(). Configure oauth_db_microsoft_client() for the selected service first. shinyOAuth obtains or renews tokens when the callback needs them. Keep the callback in the Shiny session that created it.

See also

oauth_db_fabric_api(). vignette("fabric", package = "shinyOAuthDB") has sign-in setup and a complete app.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Microsoft client configured with services = "kql":
callback <- oauth_db_fabric(auth$connection, service = "kql")
output$rows <- shiny::renderTable({
  fabricQueryR::fabric_kql_query(
    cluster = "https://example.kusto.fabric.microsoft.com",
    database = "Events",
    query = "Events | take 20",
    token = callback()
  )
})
} # }
